question: Why do periodic crystals never have five-fold symmetry?
answer: A repeating pattern needs corners that fit 360° exactly. Triangles, squares and hexagons do this, but a pentagon's 108° doesn't go into 360°, so pentagons always leave a gap or an overlap. That is why no repeating crystal can have five-fold symmetry. Only quasicrystals, whose pattern never repeats, have it.
move: A repeating pattern needs corners that fit 360° exactly; pentagons never do.

web.label: Four tiles lie round one point of a floor, each showing the corner it brings: a triangle 60°, a square 90°, a pentagon 108°, a hexagon 120°, with 360° to fill. Tapping a shape lays its copies round the point: triangles, squares and hexagons close and fill the floor with a repeating pattern; pentagons leave a 36° gap, and a fourth overlaps.

source: Veritasium, “The Infinite Pattern That Never Repeats” (YouTube, 2020)
